{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Smooth minimization with coordinate gradients: initial-distance bound for a convex objective; one coordinate of the gradient\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}FO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}O01\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}cv}

Single-objective optimization

Find an approximate global minimizer, with accuracy measured by suboptimality of the complete objective.

\textbf{Status.} Other quantified gap present

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Global minimization; task family: Single objective

\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex; geometry: Euclidean ball; geometry: Full space; smoothness: Coordinate smoothness

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} access order: First-order interface; feedback quality: Exact; interface family: Coordinate gradient; operation: Coordinate gradient; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Known exact value; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; computation: Internal arithmetic uncharged; randomization: Deterministic algorithms; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; feasibility: Required; object: Point; postprocessing: Unqueried output explicitly allowed

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Objective gap

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} aggregation: Per instance; mode: Deterministic; mode: Expectation; randomness: Algorithm private seed

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: Scalar oracle calls; precision: Bit precision not counted

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Find an approximate global minimizer, with accuracy measured by suboptimality of the complete objective.


\AtlasMath{\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The unknown differentiable convex function \AtlasInlineMath{f} satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{|\partial_jf(x+te_j)-\partial_jf(x)|\le b_j|t|} for every coordinate. A minimizer exists with \AtlasInlineMath{\|x_0-x^\star\|_2\le R}.

Unless another geometry is specified, vectors use the Euclidean norm \AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_2}, and matrices and higher derivatives use the corresponding operator norm. The assumptions hold uniformly throughout the declared domain.

Each coordinate-smoothness constant controls derivative variation along its own coordinate line. An individual \AtlasInlineMath{b_j} is not a Lipschitz constant for the full gradient.

Admissible parameter domain:


\AtlasMath{\begin{gathered}\varepsilon > 0,\quad d \ge 1,\quad b_j>0\quad(1\le j\le d),\quad R > 0\end{gathered}}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
Public numerical inputs: \AtlasInlineMath{d,\ (b_j)_{j=1}^d,\ R,\ \varepsilon,\ x_0}.

The unknown object is the objective \AtlasInlineMath{f}.

For each query, the algorithm chooses \AtlasInlineMath{x\in\mathbb R^d} and \AtlasInlineMath{j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}} and receives one scalar coordinate response.


\AtlasMath{\partial_j f(x)}


All responses come from one fixed unknown instance. The algorithm adaptively chooses query points and any indices permitted by the interface.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return a point \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d}.

The output may be unqueried or constructed from the query history, provided it is feasible. No additional function value or accuracy certificate is required.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}

\AtlasMath{\ell(I,\widehat{x})=f(\widehat{x})-f^\star}


\AtlasInlineMath{f^\star=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)}. The existence, compactness, or initial-suboptimality assumptions ensure that the optimal value in this comparison is finite.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
One scalar partial derivative at an algorithm-selected pair \AtlasInlineMath{(x,j)} costs one unit. A full gradient at one point costs \AtlasInlineMath{d}. No coordinate-update or span restriction is imposed.

Cost is bounded uniformly on every execution path. All calls used for initialization, repetition, batching, or candidate verification are counted.

Real arithmetic, precision, and storage applied to already available information are uncharged. Public geometric operations are limited to those explicitly granted by the oracle. Query complexity alone does not imply arithmetic, memory, or communication complexity.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Deterministic / Pointwise guarantee}
The algorithm uses no private random numbers. Query and stopping decisions may depend adaptively on the observed feedback.

No additional span, zero-respecting, linear-iteration, or memory restriction is imposed.

Interaction is adaptive to the feedback history. Every actual response is charged separately, including responses in parallel or batch queries. Internal real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged.

Select an algorithm using the public parameters, and then require the following for every admissible instance and response rule:


\AtlasMath{\forall I\,\forall\mathcal{O}\in\mathcal{O}(I):\ \ell(I,\widehat{x})\le\varepsilon}


The error guarantee holds for every instance; it is not averaged over an input distribution.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized / Expected loss}
Private randomization is allowed. Queries, stopping decisions, and postprocessing may adapt to observed feedback.

No additional span, zero-respecting, linear-iteration, or memory restriction is imposed.

Interaction is adaptive to the feedback history. Every actual response is charged separately, including responses in parallel or batch queries. Internal real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged.

Select an algorithm using the public parameters, and then require the following for every admissible instance and response rule:


\AtlasMath{\forall I\,\forall\mathcal{O}\in\mathcal{O}(I):\ \mathbb{E}_{A,\mathcal{O}}\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le\varepsilon}


The probability space includes the algorithm's private randomness. The instance and its admissible oracle law are fixed before randomness is averaged.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{x,\widehat{x}}: Query points and final output; their permitted spaces are specified separately by the oracle and output contracts \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f}: Unknown objective, with domain and structure specified by the model

\AtlasInlineMath{x_0}: Public initial point satisfying the stated initial-distance or initial-suboptimality condition

\AtlasInlineMath{f^\star}: Optimal value of the complete task; the oracle need not return it


\AtlasMath{f^\star=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)}


\AtlasInlineMath{x^\star}: A global minimizer whose existence is promised by the model; unique under strong convexity

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d}: Real vector space with \AtlasInlineMath{d} coordinates

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle}: Euclidean norm and inner product

\AtlasInlineMath{e_j}: \AtlasInlineMath{j}th standard basis vector \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\partial_j f}: The \AtlasInlineMath{j}th coordinate derivative of a differentiable function, returned as a scalar

\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Ambient dimension; a positive integer tracked explicitly. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{(b_j)_{j=1}^d}: Public vector of positive coordinate-smoothness constants; numerical evaluation must support vector parameters. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{b_j>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{b}: Common coordinate smoothness constant on the equal-constants slice. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{b>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Upper bound on the distance from the public initial point to a minimizer \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Target tolerance for the underlying error defined by the accuracy measure \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{c}: Sufficiently small universal positive constant, potentially different between theorems; it is not a numerical threshold. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<c<1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{C}: Sufficiently large universal constant, independent of the tracked parameters; no numerical value is specified. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{C>1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta_{\rm sum}}: Sum of the coordinate smoothness constants; convexity makes this a valid full-gradient smoothness constant.


\AtlasMath{\beta_{\rm sum}=\sum_{j=1}^d b_j}


\AtlasInlineMath{\ell}: The underlying loss or error defined by the accuracy measure; its expected, probabilistic, or worst-case aggregation is specified by the success contract

\AtlasInlineMath{I,\mathcal{O},A}: Admissible instance, a response rule consistent with that instance, and an algorithm; the algorithm is selected before the unknown instance

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O},\widetilde\Omega}: Notation for asymptotic upper and lower bounds, constant-factor matching rates, and explicitly permitted logarithmic factors. Hidden-constant dependence is specified in each regime.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log}: Natural logarithm; changing to another fixed base affects only a constant

\AtlasInlineMath{S_b}: The sum of square roots \AtlasInlineMath{\sum_j\sqrt{b_j}} is a derived quantity only.


\AtlasMath{S_b=\sum_{j=1}^d\sqrt{b_j}}


\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E}}: Expectation over the declared randomness after fixing the instance and admissible response law

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R1 - Convex initial-distance contract}
\textbf{Region.} \AtlasInlineMath{b_j>0,\quad R>0,\quad\varepsilon>0}

\textbf{Views.} Deterministic / Pointwise guarantee

\textbf{Quantity.} Q1

\textbf{Resource.} One scalar partial derivative at an algorithm-selected pair \AtlasInlineMath{(x,j)} costs one unit. A full gradient at one point costs \AtlasInlineMath{d}. No coordinate-update or span restriction is imposed.

\textbf{Status.} Other quantified gap

\textbf{Lower bound.} B11, B14

\AtlasMath{\begin{cases}0,&\varepsilon\ge\beta_{\rm sum}R^2/2,\\\max\{1,3d/4\},&b_j=b\ (\forall j),\ 0<\varepsilon\le bR^2/8,\\1,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}}
\textbf{Upper bound.} B1, B2, B10

\AtlasMath{\begin{cases}0,&\varepsilon\ge\beta_{\rm sum}R^2/2,\\\min\{Cd^2\log(2+\beta_{\rm sum}R^2/\varepsilon),CdR\sqrt{\beta_{\rm sum}/\varepsilon}\},&0<\varepsilon<\beta_{\rm sum}R^2/2.\end{cases}}
\textbf{Gap or comparison.} Exact C*=0 for epsilon>=beta\_\allowbreak{}sum R\textasciicircum{}2/2, with ratio inapplicable. Below it, divide the unchanged upper minimum by max\{1,3d/4\} on r7 and by 1 elsewhere. The dimension-dependent improvement is strict for d>=2 on r7; positive-cost gaps remain.

\textbf{Comparison argument.} Retain the original upper and zero-query branches conditionally. FO\_\allowbreak{}COORDINATE\_\allowbreak{}DIAGONAL\_\allowbreak{}DET\_\allowbreak{}Q1 applies the retained diagonal-information inequality to deterministic pointwise algorithms and yields 3d/4 scalar calls on r7, including epsilon=bR\textasciicircum{}2/8. Since beta\_\allowbreak{}sum=db there, r7 is disjoint from epsilon>=beta\_\allowbreak{}sum R\textasciicircum{}2/2. The resulting lower is max\{1,3d/4\} on r7 and one elsewhere below the zero-query threshold. The stored b3 and b4 retain quantity q2 and are excluded from this q1 bracket; no identity merger is used.

\textbf{Quantity.} Q3

\AtlasMath{\max\{cd,cR\sqrt{b/\varepsilon},1\}}
\textbf{Upper bound.} B5, B6, B7

\AtlasMath{\min\{C(1+RS_b/\sqrt\varepsilon),Cd^2\log(2+\beta_{\rm sum}R^2/\varepsilon),CdR\sqrt{\beta_{\rm sum}/\varepsilon}\}}
\textbf{Gap or comparison.} 
\AtlasMath{\frac{\min\{C(1+RS_b/\sqrt\varepsilon),Cd^2\log(2+\beta_{\rm sum}R^2/\varepsilon),CdR\sqrt{\beta_{\rm sum}/\varepsilon}\}}{\max\{cd,cR\sqrt{b/\varepsilon},1\}}}


\textbf{Comparison argument.} Compare on the intersection of O01.cv-R.parameter-domain and O01.cv-uniform-hd. The all-dimensional \AtlasInlineMath{\Omega(d)} coordinate-information lower bound strengthens the bound obtained by full-gradient simulation alone. A matching full-parameter lower bound for arbitrary queries is still unavailable. FO\_\allowbreak{}COORDINATE\_\allowbreak{}ZERO\_\allowbreak{}QUERY adds the compatible one-call lower bound. Since this regime has b\_\allowbreak{}j=b and epsilon<=c bR\textasciicircum{}2 with the baseline universal c chosen <=1/8 as permitted by FO\_\allowbreak{}COORDINATE\_\allowbreak{}SMOOTH, epsilon<beta\_\allowbreak{}sum R\textasciicircum{}2/2. Hence the zero-query upper branch is disjoint from this comparison.

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Convex differentiability and coordinate smoothness constants \$b\_\allowbreak{}j\$ imply full-gradient smoothness at most \$\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}\{\textbackslash{}rm sum\}=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}sum\_\allowbreak{}jb\_\allowbreak{}j\$. For \$C\textasciicircum{}2\$ functions the positive semidefinite Hessian has diagonal at most \$b\_\allowbreak{}j\$,\allowbreak{} and largest eigenvalue at most its trace. Convex smoothing and a limit give the differentiable case. A full gradient costs \$d\$ coordinate calls,\allowbreak{} so full-gradient acceleration and certificates acquire a factor \$d\$.\newline{}\newline{}For equal constants,\allowbreak{} let independent signs define \$v\_\allowbreak{}j=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}pm R/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}sqrt d\$,\allowbreak{} and put \$f\_\allowbreak{}v(x)=\allowbreak{}b\textbackslash{}|x-v\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2\$. A scalar coordinate derivative reveals only that coordinate's sign. Conditional on any adaptive history,\allowbreak{} unqueried signs remain uniform. The Bayes expected gap after \$T\$ calls is at least\newline{}\$\$\newline{}(bR\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2)(1-T/\allowbreak{}d).\newline{}\$\$\newline{}Error at most \$bR\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}8\$ requires \$T\textbackslash{}ge3d/\allowbreak{}4\$. For initial gap \$\textbackslash{}Delta\$,\allowbreak{} use\newline{}\$v\_\allowbreak{}j=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}pm\textbackslash{}sqrt\{2\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}(bd)\}\$,\allowbreak{} obtaining residual\newline{}\$\textbackslash{}Delta(1-T/\allowbreak{}d)\$. At \$\textbackslash{}epsilon\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}4\$,\allowbreak{} the cost is \$\textbackslash{}Omega(d)\$. The construction is \$\textbackslash{}mu\$-strongly convex if \$\textbackslash{}mu\textbackslash{}le b\$.\newline{}\newline{}This permits arbitrary randomized adaptive query points and outputs. It is specific to scalar coordinate derivatives;\allowbreak{} exact function values can encode additional information.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy If a global minimizer lies within distance \$R\$ of \$x\_\allowbreak{}0\$,\allowbreak{} query on \$B(x\_\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{}R)\$. Since \$\textbackslash{}nabla f(x\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}star)=\allowbreak{}0\$,\allowbreak{} gradients there have norm at most \$2\textbackslash{}beta R\$. The centroid certificate gives \$O(d\textbackslash{}log(2+\textbackslash{}beta R\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon))\$ gradient calls. Smoothness gives \$f(x\_\allowbreak{}0)-f\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}star\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}beta R\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2\$,\allowbreak{} including the zero-query endpoint.\newline{}\newline{}With global \$\textbackslash{}mu\$-strong convexity and initial gap \$\textbackslash{}Delta\$,\allowbreak{} use radius \$\textbackslash{}sqrt\{2\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}mu\}\$,\allowbreak{} obtaining \$O(d\textbackslash{}log(2+\textbackslash{}kappa\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon))\$. At \$\textbackslash{}mu=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}beta\$,\allowbreak{} equality in strong monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity forces \$\textbackslash{}nabla f(x)-\textbackslash{}nabla f(y)=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}beta(x-y)\$. One gradient identifies the minimizer of this known-curvature quadratic plus unknown affine term. Opposite translations exclude zero calls at nontrivial accuracy.\newline{}\newline{}Under global H{\AtlasUnicodeText ö}\allowbreak{}lder smoothness in \$\textbackslash{}ell\_\allowbreak{}q\$,\allowbreak{} convert to Euclidean quantities\newline{}\$\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}E=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu d\textasciicircum{}\{(1+\textbackslash{}nu)(1/\allowbreak{}q-1/\allowbreak{}2)\_\allowbreak{}+\}\$ and\newline{}\$R\_\allowbreak{}E=\allowbreak{}Rd\textasciicircum{}\{(1/\allowbreak{}2-1/\allowbreak{}p)\_\allowbreak{}+\}\$. Gradients on the localization ball are at most \$\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}E(2R\_\allowbreak{}E)\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}nu\$,\allowbreak{} giving\newline{}\$C\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu d\textbackslash{}log(2+\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}E R\_\allowbreak{}E\textasciicircum{}\{1+\textbackslash{}nu\}/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon)\$.\newline{}A boundary minimizer of an arbitrary constrained problem does not justify the zero-gradient premise. With two public norm-distance bounds,\allowbreak{} their intersection lies in the Euclidean ball of radius \$R\_\allowbreak{}\{2,\allowbreak{}+\}\$,\allowbreak{} while the Euclidean ball of radius \$R\_\allowbreak{}\{2,\allowbreak{}-\}\$ satisfies both promises. The former gives a certificate upper bound;\allowbreak{} embedding the one-dimensional hard family in the latter gives the logarithmic lower bound.\newline{}\newline{}For gradient-norm accuracy,\allowbreak{} use \$\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f(x)\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2\textbackslash{}le2\textbackslash{}beta(f(x)-f\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}star)\$. Under initial distance,\allowbreak{} target gap \$\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2\textbackslash{}beta)\$. Under initial gap alone,\allowbreak{} instead set\newline{}\$\$\newline{}F\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}lambda=\allowbreak{}f+\textbackslash{}lambda\textbackslash{}|x-x\_\allowbreak{}0\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}qquad\textbackslash{}lambda=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(32\textbackslash{}Delta).\newline{}\$\$\newline{}Its minimizer lies within \$8\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon\$. A certificate at gap \$\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(128\textbackslash{}beta)\$ gives \$\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla F\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}lambda(\textbackslash{}widehat x)\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}epsilon/\allowbreak{}4\$,\allowbreak{} while the public regularizer contributes at most \$\textbackslash{}epsilon/\allowbreak{}4\$. Each regularized gradient costs one original gradient,\allowbreak{} and the budget is \$O(d\textbackslash{}log(2+\textbackslash{}beta\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2))\$.\newline{}\newline{}For lower transfers,\allowbreak{} strong convexity gives \$f-f\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}star\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2\textbackslash{}mu)\$. Choose the hard subclass modulus proportional to \$\textbackslash{}epsilon/\allowbreak{}R\$,\allowbreak{} or \$\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}Delta\$,\allowbreak{} for the two respective initializations. Gradient accuracy forces constant relative gap reduction. Apply the cited deterministic chain or randomized matrix-query theorem in its original dimension window;\allowbreak{} truncate only to constructions that fit. This preserves initialization,\allowbreak{} guarantee,\allowbreak{} and algorithm scope.\newline{}\newline{}For an already strongly convex model,\allowbreak{} the gap threshold required for the lower transfer is \$\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2\textbackslash{}mu)\$,\allowbreak{} whereas the sufficient gap for the upper transfer is \$\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2\textbackslash{}beta)\$. Retain these different logarithm arguments rather than silently canceling their condition-number shift. For \$1<\textbackslash{}kappa\textbackslash{}le4\$,\allowbreak{} gradient descent and the nested one-dimensional construction yield the stated comparable near-unit denominators. At \$\textbackslash{}kappa=\allowbreak{}1\$,\allowbreak{} the known-curvature quadratic is solved in one call.\newline{}\newline{}For matching \$\textbackslash{}ell\_\allowbreak{}p\$ H{\AtlasUnicodeText ö}\allowbreak{}lder geometry,\allowbreak{} the descent model along a dual steepest-descent direction gives\newline{}\$f(x)-f\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}star\textbackslash{}ge c\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\textasciicircum{}\{-1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f(x)\textbackslash{}|\_\allowbreak{}\{p\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}star\}\textasciicircum{}\{(1+\textbackslash{}nu)/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\$.\newline{}Targeting gap \$c\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\textasciicircum{}\{-1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}\{(1+\textbackslash{}nu)/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\$ in the localization certificate therefore gives\newline{}\$C\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu d\textbackslash{}log(2+\textbackslash{}beta\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu R\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}nu/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon)\$.\par\endgroup

The centroid halfspace theorem bounds the retained volume by \$(1-e\textasciicircum{}\{-1\})\textasciicircum{}T\textbackslash{}operatorname\{vol\}(Q)\$.\newline{}\newline{}The computable certificate is\newline{}\$\$\newline{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_\allowbreak{}T=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}min\_\allowbreak{}\{\textbackslash{}lambda\textbackslash{}in\textbackslash{}Delta\_\allowbreak{}T\}\textbackslash{}max\_\allowbreak{}\{x\textbackslash{}in Q\}\textbackslash{}sum\_\allowbreak{}i\textbackslash{}lambda\_\allowbreak{}i\textbackslash{}langle g\_\allowbreak{}i,\allowbreak{}x\_\allowbreak{}i-x\textbackslash{}rangle\newline{}=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}max\_\allowbreak{}\{x\textbackslash{}in Q\}\textbackslash{}min\_\allowbreak{}i\textbackslash{}langle g\_\allowbreak{}i,\allowbreak{}x\_\allowbreak{}i-x\textbackslash{}rangle.\newline{}\$\$\newline{}The equality is convex minimax. Subgradient inequalities and convexity imply\newline{}\$f(\textbackslash{}sum\_\allowbreak{}i\textbackslash{}lambda\_\allowbreak{}ix\_\allowbreak{}i)-\textbackslash{}min\_\allowbreak{}Qf\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}Gamma\_\allowbreak{}T\$.\newline{}If \$\textbackslash{}Gamma\_\allowbreak{}T>\textbackslash{}epsilon\$,\allowbreak{} choose \$z\textbackslash{}in Q\$ with all cut margins greater than \$\textbackslash{}epsilon\$. The copy \$(1-a)z+aQ\$,\allowbreak{} where \$a=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon/\allowbreak{}[2(\textbackslash{}epsilon+LD)]\$,\allowbreak{} survives every cut. Its volume is \$a\textasciicircum{}d\textbackslash{}operatorname\{vol\}(Q)\$,\allowbreak{} contradicting centroid shrinkage once \$T>C d\textbackslash{}log(2+LD/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}epsilon)\$. If the body loses volume earlier,\allowbreak{} the same positive-volume argument already certifies the error. No function values or inscribed-ball estimate are required.\newline{}\newline{}For \$Q=\allowbreak{}RB\_\allowbreak{}p\textasciicircum{}d\$ and \$\textbackslash{}ell\_\allowbreak{}q\$-Lipschitz objectives,\allowbreak{} use \$D=\allowbreak{}2Rd\textasciicircum{}\{(1/\allowbreak{}q-1/\allowbreak{}p)\_\allowbreak{}+\}\$. Returning the center has error at most \$LRd\textasciicircum{}\{(1/\allowbreak{}q-1/\allowbreak{}p)\_\allowbreak{}+\}\$,\allowbreak{} giving the coarse zero-query regime. Exact centroid,\allowbreak{} minimax,\allowbreak{} and public geometric calculations are uncharged internal operations.\newline{}\newline{}For a deterministic selector with total movement at most \$W(T)\$ on nested convex sets,\allowbreak{} instead impose deep cuts of margin \$2LW(T)/\allowbreak{}T\$. If all \$T\$ sets are nonempty,\allowbreak{} every move has length at least \$2W(T)/\allowbreak{}T\$,\allowbreak{} contradicting the movement bound. At the first empty intersection,\allowbreak{} minimax gives error at most \$2LW(T)/\allowbreak{}T\$. Substitution of the cited stable-movement theorem yields the recorded nondual upper bound. Its deterministic information scope is distinct from the scope of randomized implementations.\par\endgroup

Returning x0 uses zero queries and meets both guarantees for epsilon>=\allowbreak{}BR\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2.
